text:
Fuel cell, using hydrogen and oxygen as fuels,

A. has been used in spaceship

B. has an efficiency of $40%$ to produce electricity

C. uses aluminum as catalysts

D. is eco-friendly

E. is actually a type of Galvanic cell only

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A is correct: $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$–$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}$ fuel cells were used as the source of electrical power in the Apollo space programme.

Statement B is incorrect: a fuel cell converts the energy of the reaction directly into electricity with an efficiency of about $70%$; about $40%$ is the efficiency of thermal power plants.

Statement C is incorrect: the electrodes are porous carbon containing finely divided platinum or palladium as catalyst, not aluminium.

Statement D is correct: the overall reaction $2~\mathrm{H}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$ gives only water, so the cell is pollution free.

Statement E is correct: a fuel cell is a galvanic cell in which the reactants are supplied continuously and the energy of combustion of the fuel is converted directly into electrical energy.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Match List I with List II

  
    
    LIST I
    
    LIST II
  

  
    A.
    $α$ - Glucose and $α$ - Galactose
    I.
    Functional isomers
  
  
    B.	
    $α$ - Glucose and $β$ - Glucose
    II.
    Homologous  
  
  
    C.
    $α$ - Glucose and $α$ - Fructose
    III.
    Anomers
  
  
    D.
    $α$ - Glucose and $α$ - Ribose
    IV.
    Epimers
  

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$α$-Glucose and $α$-galactose are both aldohexoses that differ only in the configuration at C-4, so they are epimers: A–IV.

$α$-Glucose and $β$-glucose differ only in the configuration at the anomeric carbon C-1, so they are anomers: B–III.

$α$-Glucose (an aldohexose, $-\mathrm{CHO}$) and $α$-fructose (a ketohexose, $>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$) have the same formula $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}$ but different functional groups, so they are functional isomers: C–I.

$α$-Glucose ($\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{12}\mathrm{O}{}_{6}$, aldohexose) and $α$-ribose ($\mathrm{C}{}_{5}\mathrm{H}{}_{10}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$, aldopentose) belong to the same aldose series and differ by one $\mathrm{CHOH}$ unit, so they are homologous: D–II.

The matching is A–IV, B–III, C–I, D–II.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: If an iron (III) complex with the formula $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{NH}_{3})_{x}(\mathrm{CN})_{y}]^{-}$ has no electron in its $e_{g}$ orbital, then the value of $x+y$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Iron(III) is $3d^{5}$. No electron in the $e_{g}$ set means the configuration $t_{2g}^{5}e_{g}^{0}$, which arises only in a low-spin octahedral complex (strong-field $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ forces pairing), so the coordination number is 6:

$x+y=6$

With neutral $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ ligands, the charge balance is $+3-y=-1\Rightarrow y=4$, so $x=2$ and the complex is $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}(\mathrm{CN}){}_{4}]{}^{-}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: The number of unpaired d-electrons in $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}]^{3+}$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First, let us determine the $d$-electron count of the cobalt center in $\left [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}\right ]^{3+}$.

1. Oxidation state and $d$-electron count
Neutral cobalt (Co) has an atomic number of 27 and an electronic configuration:  

$\mathrm{Co}\left [\mathrm{Ar}\right ]3d^{7}4s^{2}.$  

In the +3 oxidation state, cobalt has lost a total of 3 electrons:

First two electrons are removed from the $4s$ orbital.

The third electron is removed from the $3d$ orbitals.

Thus, $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ has

$3d^{7-1}=3d^{6}.$

So in $\left [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}\right ]^{3+}$, the cobalt center is $d^{6}$.

2. High-spin vs Low-spin for $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$
Even though $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is generally considered a weak field ligand, the $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ ion has a relatively high charge (+3). A higher charge on the metal center usually increases the ligand-field splitting ($\Delta _{\mathrm{o}}$) significantly compared to lower oxidation states of the same metal.  

In most typical octahedral complexes of $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$, the splitting $\Delta _{\mathrm{o}}$ is large enough that the complex ends up being low spin.  

Electronic configuration in an octahedral field
For a $d^{6}$ octahedral low-spin complex, all six electrons pair up in the lower-energy $\mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}$ orbitals:

$\mathrm{t}_{2\mathrm{g}}^{6}\mathrm{e}_{\mathrm{g}}^{0}$

That leaves 0 unpaired electrons.

3. Final answer
Therefore, the number of unpaired $d$-electrons in  

$\left [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{6}\right ]^{3+}$ is $0.$

Correct Option: A (0)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Alcoholic KOH on heating brings about E2 dehydrohalogenation: a $β$-hydrogen and $\mathrm{Br}$ are removed from adjacent carbons to form a $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ bond.

The substrate $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CHBr}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ has two kinds of $β$-hydrogen: the benzylic $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ hydrogens and the tertiary $\mathrm{CH}$ hydrogen of the isopropyl group.

Loss of a benzylic hydrogen gives $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, whose double bond is conjugated with the benzene ring; the benzylic hydrogen is also the more acidic one, and the ring stabilises the developing double bond in the transition state.


[IMG]

Loss of the isopropyl hydrogen would give the trisubstituted alkene $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}$, stabilised only by hyperconjugation; conjugation with the aromatic ring outweighs one extra alkyl group, so the conjugated alkene is the major product.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: The correct order of the first ionization enthalpy is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First ionization enthalpies of group 13 elements ($\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): B 801, Al 577, Ga 579, In 558, Tl 589.

The fall from B to Al follows the large increase in atomic size. In Ga the ten 3d electrons shield the nucleus poorly, so its valence electron feels a higher effective nuclear charge and Ga is slightly above Al.

In Tl the poorly shielding 4f and 5d electrons (lanthanoid contraction) raise the effective nuclear charge further, so Tl has the highest value after B.

Thus $\mathrm{Tl}\quad (589)>\mathrm{Ga}(579)>\mathrm{Al}(577)$; option (D) fails because Ga is above Al.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : The correct order of first ionization enthalpy values of $\mathrm{Li},\mathrm{Na},\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ is $\mathrm{Na}<\mathrm{Li}<\mathrm{Cl}<\mathrm{F}$.

Statement II : The correct order of negative electron gain enthalpy values of $\mathrm{Li},\mathrm{Na},\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ is $\mathrm{Na}<\mathrm{Li}<\mathrm{F}<\mathrm{Cl}$

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
First ionisation enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) are Na $496$, Li $520$, Cl $1256$, F $1681$: ionisation enthalpy falls down a group, and the halogens, with far higher effective nuclear charge, lie well above the alkali metals. So $\mathrm{Na}<\mathrm{Li}<\mathrm{Cl}<\mathrm{F}$ and Statement I is true.

Electron gain enthalpies (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) are Na $-53$, Li $-60$, F $-328$, Cl $-349$. The added electron is farther from the nucleus in Na than in Li, and it suffers strong repulsion in the compact $2p$ shell of F, so the negative electron gain enthalpies follow $\mathrm{Na}<\mathrm{Li}<\mathrm{F}<\mathrm{Cl}$ and Statement II is true.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: For a strong electrolyte, a plot of molar conductivity against (concentration) ${}^{1/2}$ is a straight line, with a negative slope, the correct unit for the slope is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a strong electrolyte, molar conductivity varies with concentration as

$\Lambda _{m}=\Lambda _{m}^{\circ }-Ac^{1/2}$

so the slope of the plot of $\Lambda _{m}$ against $c^{1/2}$ is $-A$, and the unit of the slope is the unit of $\Lambda _{m}$ divided by the unit of $c^{1/2}$.

Unit of $\Lambda _{m}$: $\text{S cm}^{2}\text{mol}^{-1}$; unit of $c^{1/2}$: $(\text{mol L}^{-1})^{1/2}=\text{mol}^{1/2}\text{L}^{-1/2}$.

$\text{Unit of slope}=\dfrac{\text{S cm}^{2}\text{mol}^{-1}}{\text{mol}^{1/2}\text{L}^{-1/2}}=\text{S cm}^{2}\text{mol}^{-3/2}\text{L}^{1/2}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: When $\mathrm{MnO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ are added to a salt $(\mathrm{A})$, a greenish yellow gas is liberated. The salt (A) is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A greenish-yellow gas liberated by $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}$ is $\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$, formed when $\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}$ oxidises chloride ion in the acid medium:

$2~\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}+\mathrm{MnO}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}\longrightarrow (\mathrm{NH}{}_{4}){}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{MnSO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Under the same conditions $\mathrm{NaBr}$ gives reddish-brown $\mathrm{Br}{}_{2}$ vapours, $\mathrm{CaI}{}_{2}$ gives violet $\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$ vapours and $\mathrm{KNO}{}_{3}$ gives no greenish-yellow gas.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
The correct statement/s about Hydrogen bonding is/are

A. Hydrogen bonding exists when H is covalently bonded to the highly electronegative atom.

B. Intermolecular H bonding is present in $o$-nitro phenol

C. Intramolecular $\mathrm{H}$ bonding is present in HF.

D. The magnitude of $\mathrm{H}$ bonding depends on the physical state of the compound.

E. H-bonding has powerful effect on the structure and properties of compounds

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom such as F, O or N, so statement A is correct.

In $o$-nitrophenol the $-\mathrm{OH}$ and $-\mathrm{NO}_{2}$ groups are on adjacent carbon atoms, so the hydrogen bond forms within the same molecule (intramolecular), not between molecules; statement B is incorrect.

In $\mathrm{HF}$ the H of one molecule is hydrogen-bonded to the F of a neighbouring molecule, giving zig-zag chains (intermolecular); statement C is incorrect.

The magnitude of hydrogen bonding depends on the physical state of the compound: it is maximum in the solid state and minimum in the gaseous state, so statement D is correct.

Hydrogen bonding strongly influences structure and properties such as boiling point, solubility and the open cage structure of ice, so statement E is correct.

The correct statements are A, D and E.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: Choose the Incorrect Statement about Dalton's Atomic Theory
options: Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in any ratio.
chemical reactions involve reorganization of atoms
All the atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dalton's atomic theory states that matter consists of indivisible atoms, that all atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass, that compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio, and that chemical reactions involve only the reorganisation of atoms.

Statements (B), (C) and (D) are therefore postulates of the theory. The later discovery of subatomic particles does not change the fact that (B) is what Dalton proposed.

Statement (A) says that atoms combine in any ratio, which contradicts the fixed-ratio postulate, so (A) is the incorrect statement.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text:
The number of species from the following that have pyramidal geometry around the central atom is $_________$

$\mathrm{S}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}^{2-},\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-},\mathrm{SO}_{3}^{2-},\mathrm{S}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{7}^{2-}$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The geometry around the central atom follows from its number of bond pairs and lone pairs (VSEPR theory).

In $\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ the central S is bonded to three O atoms and one S atom and has no lone pair, so it is tetrahedral.

In $\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$ the S atom is bonded to four O atoms and has no lone pair, so it is tetrahedral.

In $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ the S atom is bonded to three O atoms and carries one lone pair ($\mathrm{sp}^{3}$), so it is trigonal pyramidal.


[IMG]

In $\mathrm{S}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{7}{}^{2-}$ each S atom is bonded to four O atoms (one of them the bridging O) and has no lone pair, so each S is tetrahedral.

Only $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}{}^{2-}$ has pyramidal geometry, so the number of such species is 1.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

text: A first row transition metal in its +2 oxidation state has a spin-only magnetic moment value of $3.86\mathrm{BM}$. The atomic number of the metal is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the atomic number of the metal based on the provided spin-only magnetic moment value, we use the formula for calculating the spin-only magnetic moment:

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}μ_{B}$

where $μ$ is the magnetic moment in Bohr magnetons ($μ_{B}$), and $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Given that the spin-only magnetic moment value is $3.86\mathrm{BM}$, we can set this value equal to the formula to solve for $n$:

$3.86=\sqrt{n(n+2)}$

Squaring both sides gives:

$14.8996=n(n+2)$

Since $n$ must be an integer and this equation doesn't solve neatly for an integer $n$, we look for a value of $n$ that would give a product close to $14.8996$ when plugged into $\sqrt{n(n+2)}$.

Practically, we can test the square root values near $3.86$ for different $n$ to see which one gives a close match. Considering the usual spin-only magnetic moments for common numbers of unpaired electrons:

$n=1$, $μ=\sqrt{3}\approx 1.73μ_{B}$

$n=2$, $μ=\sqrt{8}\approx 2.83μ_{B}$

$n=3$, $μ=\sqrt{15}\approx 3.87μ_{B}$

$n=4$, $μ=\sqrt{24}\approx 4.90μ_{B}$

The value $n=3$ gives a magnetic moment of approximately $3.87μ_{B}$, which is very close to the given value, $3.86μ_{B}$. Therefore, the metal has 3 unpaired electrons in its d-orbital configuration.

In the +2 oxidation state, metals lose electrons from the s-orbital before the d-orbital. Given that the element is a first row transition metal, starting with scandium (Sc) at atomic number 21 which has an electronic configuration of $[Ar]3d^{1}4s^{2}$ in its neutral state, we can deduce the configurations:

$Z=22$ for Titanium (Ti), which has a neutral configuration of $[Ar]3d^{2}4s^{2}$. In the +2 oxidation state, it would have an electronic configuration of $[Ar]3d^{2}$, resulting in 2 unpaired electrons.

$Z=23$ for Vanadium (V), with a neutral configuration of $[Ar]3d^{3}4s^{2}$. In the +2 state, its configuration would be $[Ar]3d^{3}$, presenting 3 unpaired electrons, which matches our calculation.

$Z=26$ for Iron (Fe), indicating a neutral configuration of $[Ar]3d^{6}4s^{2}$. In the +2 state, $[Ar]3d^{6}$, which would have 4 unpaired electrons, not matching the calculation.

$Z=25$ for Manganese (Mn), with a neutral configuration of $[Ar]3d^{5}4s^{2}$. In the +2 state, $[Ar]3d^{5}$, indicating 5 unpaired electrons, which also does not match our calculation.

So, the atomic number of the metal with a +2 oxidation state and a spin-only magnetic moment value of $3.86\mathrm{BM}$ (corresponding to 3 unpaired electrons) is 23, which identifies the metal as Vanadium (V). Therefore,

Option B (23) is the correct answer.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift

The equilibrium constant for the reaction

$\mathrm{SO}_{3}(\mathrm{g})⇌\mathrm{SO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

is $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=4.9\times 10^{-2}$. The value of $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}$ for the reaction given below $2\mathrm{SO}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{SO}_{3}(\mathrm{g})$ is :

text: From $6.55\mathrm{g}$ of aniline, the maximum amount of acetanilide that can be prepared will be $________$ $\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{g}$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the maximum amount of acetanilide that can be prepared from 6.55 g of aniline, we need to use stoichiometry. Let's go through the process step by step.

1. Molecular weights calculation:

The molecular weight of aniline $(C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2})$ is calculated as follows:

$\text{Molecular weight of aniline}=6\times 12+5\times 1+14+2\times 1=93\text{g/mol}$

The molecular weight of acetanilide $(C_{8}H_{9}$NO) is calculated as follows:

$\text{Molecular weight of acetanilide}=8\times 12+9\times 1+14+16=135\text{g/mol}$

2. Mole calculation:

Moles of aniline:

$\text{Moles of aniline}=\frac{\text{Mass of aniline}}{\text{Molecular weight of aniline}}=\frac{6.55\text{g}}{93\text{g/mol}}=0.0704\text{mol}$

3. Stoichiometry of the reaction:

The reaction between aniline and acetic anhydride to form acetanilide follows a 1:1 mole ratio.

4. Mass calculation:

Theoretical mass of acetanilide formed:

$\text{Mass of acetanilide}=\text{Moles of aniline}\times \text{Molecular weight of acetanilide}=0.0704\text{mol}\times 135\text{g/mol}=9.504\text{g}$

5. Convert to the desired unit:

Given the unit required is $\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{g}$, we express 9.504 g as:

$9.504\text{g}=95.04\times 10^{-1}\text{g}$

Therefore, the maximum amount of acetanilide that can be prepared from 6.55 g of aniline is $95.04\times 10^{-1}\mathrm{g}$.

text:
Consider the following reaction, the rate expression of which is given below

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}\to \mathrm{C} \\ \text{rate}=\mathrm{k}[\mathrm{A}]^{1/2}[\mathrm{B}]^{1/2} \end{array}$

The reaction is initiated by taking $1\mathrm{M}$ concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$ each. If the rate constant $(\mathrm{k})$ is $4.6\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$, then the time taken for $\mathrm{A}$ to become $0.1\mathrm{M}$ is $_________ \sec $.
(nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} A+B\to C \\ \dfrac{-d[A]}{dt}=k[A]^{1/2}[B]^{1/2} \end{array}$

Since, $[A]=[B]$

$\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow \dfrac{-d[A]}{dt}=k[A] \\ \Rightarrow kt=\ln \dfrac{[A]_{0}}{[A]} \\ \Rightarrow t=\dfrac{1}{4.6\times 10^{-2}}\times \ln \left (\dfrac{1}{0.1}\right ) \\ =\dfrac{2.303}{4.6}\times 100\approx 50 \end{array}$

text: Vanillin compound obtained from vanilla beans, has total sum of oxygen atoms and $π$ electrons is $__________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To determine the total sum of oxygen atoms and $π$ electrons in vanillin, let's first consider the structure of vanillin. Vanillin is an organic compound with the chemical formula $C_{8}H_{8}O_{3}$. It consists of a benzene ring attached to a methoxy group (-OCH$_{3}), a$ hydroxyl group (-OH), and an aldehyde group (-CHO).

Firstly, let's count the oxygen atoms:

One from the methoxy group (-OCH$_{3})$

One from the hydroxyl group (-OH)

One from the aldehyde group (-CHO)

Thus, there are a total of 3 oxygen atoms in vanillin.

Next, let's calculate the total number of $π$ electrons:

The benzene ring has 3 double bonds, contributing 6 $π$ electrons.

The aldehyde group has 1 double bond (C=O), contributing 2 $π$ electrons.

The methoxy group and the hydroxyl group do not contribute any $π$ electrons since they do not have $π$ bonds in their structures.

Therefore, vanillin has a total of 8 $π$ electrons from the benzene ring and the aldehyde group.

Adding the number of oxygen atoms (3) and the $π$ electrons (8) gives us a total sum of 11.

Thus, the total sum of oxygen atoms and $π$ electrons in vanillin is 11.

text:
Phthalimide is made to undergo following sequence of reactions.


[IMG]


Total number of $π$ bonds present in product 'P' is/are $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
KOH removes the acidic N–H proton of phthalimide, giving potassium phthalimide; the phthalimide anion then displaces $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$ from benzyl chloride ($\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}}2$), giving N-benzylphthalimide (P).


[IMG]

$π$ bonds in P: the two $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$ groups give 2, the benzene ring of the phthalimide unit gives 3 and the phenyl ring of the benzyl group gives 3.

Total number of $π$ bonds $=2+3+3=8$.

Hence, the answer is 8.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2024 (Online) 4th April Evening Shift
